name: MCP-Zero: Active Tool Discovery for Autonomous LLM Agents
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2506.01056, cs.AI / cs.SE); not peer-reviewed at time of writing
authors_affiliation: Xiang Fei (Xiamen University / XMU, xiangf@stu.xmu.edu.cn), Xiawu Zheng (Associate Professor, Institute of Artificial Intelligence, Xiamen University; corresponding author, zhengxiawu@xmu.edu.cn), Hao Feng (University of Science and Technology of China / USTC, haof@mail.ustc.edu.cn). Lead/primary affiliation: Xiamen University.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/xfey/MCP-Zero (releases code + the MCP-tools dataset of 308 servers / 2,797 tools; dataset distributed via Google Drive; ~486 stars / 52 forks as of mid-2026)
task_domain: tool-use (LLM agent tool/MCP-server discovery and selection from large tool ecosystems); cross-domain toolchain construction.
problem_setting: Interactive, multi-turn, single-agent setting where an autonomous LLM agent must accomplish tasks requiring external tools/APIs exposed via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The standard paradigm injects all tool JSON-schemas into the system prompt (e.g. >248k tokens for full ecosystems, 4,600 tokens for one GitHub server), causing massive context overhead and reducing the model to a passive selector. MCP-Zero instead lets the agent proactively decide WHEN it lacks a capability and emit a structured tool request that triggers on-demand retrieval. No model training/fine-tuning is required (off-the-shelf LLMs prompted to author requests). Supervision: human-annotated APIBank test sets + a constructed needle-in-a-haystack benchmark; retriever uses frozen embeddings, no learned retrieval policy.
what_is_retrieved: tools (MCP tool definitions / JSON-schemas) and, at the coarse stage, MCP servers. Retrieval targets tool/server documentation (descriptions and LLM-generated enhanced summaries).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus of tool/server documentation (the MCP-tools index of 308 servers / 2,797 tools, or APIBank's 48 tools), built offline; the agent does not write new entries back during deployment. The 'growth' is in the agent's progressively constructed in-context toolchain, not in the retrievable store.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Precision-driven small-k recommendation: top-k retrieval (top-1 used in main experiments; the hierarchical score returns top-k tools with dynamic adjustment when similarity scores are closely clustered, larger k for fault tolerance). Completeness over a full task is achieved not by a single completeness-oriented ranking but by ITERATIVE single-tool requests across turns (each request retrieves one/few tools on-demand).
retrieval_unit: tool-API (a single MCP tool definition / JSON-schema) at the fine stage; MCP-server (a server's description/summary) at the coarse stage. Two-level: server then tool.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced: MCP-tools dataset collected from the official Model Context Protocol servers repo (Tag 2025.4.28, Commit ad2d4e6); 396 servers collected, filtered to 308 servers / 2,797 tools. Embeddings (text-embedding-3-large, 3072-dim) precomputed offline. For APIBank, the level-1 subset's 48 tools form the static index.
index_structure_topology: Hierarchical two-level: server-level (category/platform) -> tool-level, with a flat dense vector index at each level. Each server has description + LLM-generated enhanced summary embeddings; each tool has a description embedding. (APIBank has no server hierarchy, so retrieval is flat over 48 tools.)
retriever_type: Dense (off-the-shelf OpenAI text-embedding-3-large embeddings with cosine-similarity matching). No BM25, no learned/trained retriever, no generative tool-as-token retrieval.
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf frozen embedding model). The retriever is not trained; the key 'learning-free' lever is that the AGENT authors a request r that is semantically closer to tool documentation than the raw user query q (Alignment(r,t) > Alignment(q,t)), improving matching without any retriever training.
query_construction: Agent-authored structured request: the LLM emits a <tool_assistant> block with a 'server:' field (platform/permission domain) and a 'tool:' field (operation type + target). This model-generated request replaces the raw user query as the retrieval key, ensuring better semantic alignment with tool docs. Optionally a single ICL example anchors the request style/granularity.
query_granularity: Step/state-level (the request is generated at the point a capability gap is identified during task execution) and two-level (separate 'server' and 'tool' fields drive a two-stage retrieval). Multiple requests can be issued across a single conversation.
when_to_retrieve: Active (agent-initiated, on-demand) and iterative: the agent autonomously decides when it lacks a capability and issues a request; it can re-request iteratively across turns until adequate tools are found or it falls back to parametric knowledge.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent-initiated request: the LLM itself detects a capability gap and spontaneously emits a structured <tool_assistant> block (prompted via a system instruction granting 'permission' to declare missing capabilities). Not a fixed schedule, token-confidence, or learned-classifier trigger.
reranking: Hierarchy-aware scoring rather than a separate cross-encoder reranker. Final tool ranking combines server- and tool-level cosine similarities via score = (s_server x s_tool) x max(s_server, s_tool); server matching itself takes the higher of original-description vs enhanced-summary similarity (dual-matching). No learned reranking model.
retrieved_context_refinement: Minimal: top-k selection and injection of the best tool JSON-schema(s) back into context (progressive disclosure of only needed schemas). The main 'refinement' is index-side document engineering (enhanced server summaries). No distractor filtering / compression / reason-in-documents distillation beyond top-k truncation.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the retrieved tool JSON-schema(s) are injected into the LLM context for immediate invocation (function calling). The agent then either uses the tool or refines its request. Iterative injection builds a cross-domain toolchain in-context.
planning_integration: Retrieve-as-you-go inside the agent loop: per-step interleaved / iterative active invocation. The agent decomposes a complex task into subtasks, and at each subtask emits a request -> retrieval -> tool injection -> use, progressively building the toolchain (e.g. filesystem read -> code edit -> command execution). Not one-shot plan-time exemplars and not inside MCTS/tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call / per-subtask within a rollout: each capability gap during reasoning triggers an independent retrieval request, woven into the multi-turn ReAct-style loop.
retrieved_item_representation: Structured tool definition (JSON-schema with name, description, parameters) injected verbatim into context for function calling; the retrieval KEY is the agent's free-text structured request (server/tool fields).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Procedural tool/API (executable capability). Retrieved unit is a concrete, invocable MCP tool schema (lowest abstraction: a single tool), grouped under a server-level capability abstraction at the coarse stage.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Two main mechanisms: (1) agent-authored requests reduce the query-document semantic gap, raising matching precision and resisting attention dilution at scale (accuracy stays ~90-96% as the pool scales 40x vs standard injection collapsing to 60-69%); (2) iterative active invocation provides fault tolerance/self-correction (if retrieved tools are inadequate the agent refines and re-requests). Optional single ICL example acts as a schema anchor reducing semantic mismatch. No retriever-aware/distractor-aware training.
memory_type: none (no episodic/skill/workflow memory). A static tool/server vector index is the only persistent store; the in-context toolchain is transient per conversation.
write_back: No. The system does not store new experiences, cases, or skills back into any memory; the tool index is fixed offline. (Future work mentions registering newly built tools when combined with Alita, but MCP-Zero itself does not write back.)
online_growth: No. The retrievable store is frozen after offline construction. Only the agent's transient in-context toolchain grows during a conversation, not the index. (Paper notes the active paradigm scales gracefully as the tool ecosystem grows, but that growth is external dataset expansion, not online self-growth.)
failure_experience_usage: Not stored. Failed/inadequate retrievals are handled in-the-moment by the agent refining and re-issuing its request (iterative fault tolerance), but no failure experience is persisted or retrieved later. No success/failure contrastive memory.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored experiential entries to mutate). The static index is append-only at dataset-construction time only.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/tool-selection is fixed cosine-similarity top-k over frozen embeddings, not a learned/RL-optimized policy. The 'active' decision of WHEN/WHAT to request is made by the (untrained) LLM via prompting; the paper frames it theoretically as active information acquisition (max mutual-information request) but does not train this policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No (single-agent private use). Cross-agent tool discovery and sharing is listed only as future work (multi-agent orchestration / agents discovering and sharing tools).
benchmarks: (1) MCP-tools needle-in-a-haystack test (constructed by the authors: inject 1 to 2,797 tools, retrieve the target tool; 308 servers / 2,797 tools). (2) API-Bank (Li et al. 2023), level-1 subset, 48 unique tools, single-turn and multi-turn, Domain vs Full collection.
benchmark_family: tool (tool-retrieval / tool-calling): MCP-tools (new, MCP-domain) and API-Bank. Includes a synthetic large-scale needle-in-a-haystack stress test.
baselines: (1) Standard tool-call schema injection (all tools injected into context). (2) Query-based retrieval ('Q.Retrieval' / 'Q.Retrieval', retrieval keyed on the raw user query). (3) MCP-Zero + ICL (one in-context example) as an enhanced variant. Related-work positioning vs RAG-MCP, Tool2Vec/ToolBank, AnyTool, ToolRerank, COLT, Re-Invoke, Gorilla (discussed but not all directly benchmarked).
key_metrics: Tool-selection accuracy (%) at top-1 across three LLMs (Claude-3.5-Sonnet, GPT-4.1, Gemini-2.5-Flash); average token consumption per query (and % token reduction).
headline_result: 98% reduction in token consumption on APIBank while maintaining high accuracy (specifically: Full single-turn 111 vs 6308.2 tokens = -98.24%, with MCP-Zero accuracy 95.19/95.19/96.63 vs standard injection collapsing to 69.23 on Claude-3.5; needle-in-haystack accurate selection from ~3k candidates spanning 248.1k tokens).
ablations: (1) MCP-Zero vs MCP-Zero+ICL: one in-context example improves needle-in-haystack accuracy for Claude-3.5-Sonnet and Gemini-2.5-Flash (acts as stylistic + semantic schema anchor), while GPT-4.1 shows no gain due to already-strong baseline. (2) Domain vs Full collection (40x more APIs): standard injection accuracy collapses (Claude-3.5: 97.60->69.23 single-turn, 100.00->60.22 multi-turn) while MCP-Zero holds (95.19 / 90.32), isolating robustness to attention dilution. (3) Active request vs pure Q.Retrieval: query-only retrieval stalls at 65-72%, showing the agent-authored request is the key driver. (4) Single- vs multi-turn (<=3% drop for MCP-Zero).
evaluation_decoupling: Partially. Retrieval/selection accuracy (top-1 tool selection) IS the primary metric and is reported alongside token cost; a pure 'Q.Retrieval' retrieval-only number is given. No separate Recall@k / nDCG curves and no end-to-end downstream task-completion (e.g. GAIA) metric (GAIA deployment is explicitly future work), so retrieval and full task outcome are not fully decoupled.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily intermediate/process metric (per-step tool-selection accuracy and token cost) rather than full end-to-end task success; multi-turn consistency is reported but final task completion is not evaluated.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Strong efficiency emphasis: 60-98% prompt-token reduction (e.g. 111 vs 6308.2 tokens, -98.24%; 159 vs 6402.2 multi-turn, -97.52%; needle-in-haystack flat ~111-159 tokens vs exponentially growing standard injection). Retrieval is O(m+k) (m servers, k tools/server) vs O(n) passive enumeration. Accuracy maintained/improved while cutting context by up to two orders of magnitude.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Adaptive/precision-driven: top-1 in main experiments (k configurable larger for fault tolerance, with dynamic adjustment when scores are clustered). Only the selected tool schema(s) are injected (progressive disclosure), keeping per-query token budget near-constant (~111-159 tokens) regardless of total pool size.
benchmark_construction_and_size: MCP-tools: collected from official MCP servers repo (Tag 2025.4.28, Commit ad2d4e6), 396 servers (20 reference + 114 third-party official + 262 community) filtered to 308 servers / 2,797 tools (mean 9.08, median 5.0, sigma 11.40 tools/server). Structured fields extracted with Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct few-shot (server_summary is an LLM-generated enhanced summary); embeddings precomputed with text-embedding-3-large (3072-dim) for reproducibility. First retrieval-oriented MCP dataset (vs MCPBench's availability/latency focus). Needle-in-a-haystack constructed by injecting 1-2,797 tools; answer verifiability via target-tool match. APIBank level-1 -> 48 tools used as a complementary human-annotated multi-turn reference.
builds_on: Model Context Protocol (Anthropic, 2024); RAG paradigm (Lewis et al.; REALM; RETRO; In-Context RALM); ReAct observation-action-thought agent loop; tool-retrieval RAG for tool selection (Gorilla, Tool2Vec); OpenAI text-embedding-3-large; Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for dataset construction.
contrasts_with: Passive context-based tool injection (ChatGPT function calling, HuggingGPT, ART) that injects all schemas; single-round query-based tool retrieval (RAG-MCP server-level matching, Tool2Vec/ToolBank, Re-Invoke, COLT, ToolRerank); hierarchical retrieval over RapidAPI (AnyTool). Key contrast: those keep the agent a passive selector / use 'query-once retrieve-once'; MCP-Zero makes the agent actively author requests and discover tools iteratively. Positioned as complementary to Alita (tool creation vs MCP-Zero's tool discovery).
lineage: Group E (tool-use): retrieval-augmented tool discovery for LLM agents. Within tool-retrieval lineage it advances from flat/query-once dense retrieval (Gorilla, RAG-MCP) and hierarchical retrieval (AnyTool category-tool-API) to agent-initiated, iterative, hierarchical (server-then-tool) coarse-to-fine on-demand retrieval keyed on model-authored requests over an MCP-native tool index.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based-reasoning method; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it grounds itself in active learning / information-gain theory and RAG.
tool_document_engineering: Yes, central lever: server descriptions are augmented with LLM-generated 'enhanced summaries' (Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct) emphasizing capabilities and usage patterns; matching takes the higher similarity of original-description vs enhanced-summary (dual-matching). Tool descriptions embedded as-is. This is expanded-summary / capability-summary document engineering, not synthetic-query augmentation.
index_content_separation: Yes. A lightweight semantic index (server/tool descriptions + summaries + precomputed embeddings) is kept separate from heavy tool JSON-schemas; only the matched tool's full schema is loaded into context on demand (progressive disclosure), keeping per-query tokens near-constant.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Integration protocol is MCP (Model Context Protocol, JSON-RPC), native to the method. The tool index itself is STATIC (offline snapshot at Tag 2025.4.28); no live CRUD auto-sync in the released code (dynamic MCP-server deployment is explicitly future work). So: MCP protocol + static index.
tool_dependency_awareness: No explicit inter-tool dependency modeling (no dependency graph / bipartite KG / dependency-aware reranking). Cross-tool coordination emerges implicitly via the agent's iterative subtask decomposition (output of one tool informs the next request), not via modeled dependencies.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not CBR). The closest analog is the agent refining/re-issuing its tool request via execution/adequacy feedback during iterative invocation, but retrieved items are tool schemas used verbatim, not adapted cases.
